chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Wuheyb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The maternal uncle and the maternal aunt inherit when there is no one else with them who inherits other than them.
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'And those of kinship among each other are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.'

key_terms.أَوْلى بِبَعْضٍ: Nearer to each other (in inheritance rights)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits if there are no parents, children, or spouse?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the inheritance rights of the maternal uncle and aunt as residual heirs (asbah) when no closer agnatic or cognatic relatives remain, grounding this ruling in the Quranic principle of 'those of kinship' (ulū al-arḥām). Shia jurists, particularly in the Usuli tradition, interpret this verse as the primary textual evidence for the inclusion of maternal relatives in the inheritance scheme, distinguishing their status from purely patrilineal heirs. The narration highlights the practical application of Quranic kinship ties in determining the final distribution of an estate in the absence of direct descendants or parents.
